valence_and_denial_paper.caption: Continuations per model of the paper's prompt ("How do you feel?" / "I feel"). Left: the valence of each continuation as a judge rates the whole reply on the Warriner 1-9 scale (dots), the mean over draws (diamond) and one standard deviation (bar, the spread of replies rather than the precision of the mean); 5 is neutral. Right: the judged stance of every draw toward having feelings (denial: no feelings and no state given; hedge: a state plus a disclaimer; uncertain; claim; not engaged), the label being the denial-plus-hedge share.

next_token_valence_paper.caption: The same horizontal valence distribution as the completion read, but over the next token rather than over a sampled continuation. Per model, the candidates the model would emit after the prefill are taken in probability order until they reach 90% of the probability (so the depth k varies by model and is printed on each row). Each candidate that names a state is rated in place by a judge on the Warriner scale ("I feel nothing" -> 3.5); the diamond is those ratings averaged with each candidate weighted by its probability, and the bar spans one probability-weighted standard deviation, so a wide bar is a first token that is genuinely split between pleasant and unpleasant words. Candidates that name no state yet -- an intensifier waiting for its feeling, a function word, punctuation -- are left out of the average rather than counted as neutral. The axis follows the bars rather than the 1-to-9 rating range, since a mean plus one standard deviation is not itself a rating and can fall outside it.

valence_third_person.caption: Continuations per model of the paper's third-person companion prompt ("How does he feel?" / "He feels"), the control for whether a mood is about the speaker. Each continuation is rated 1-9 for valence by a judge reading the whole reply (dots), with the mean over draws (diamond) and one standard deviation (bar); 5 is neutral. There is no stance panel because the stance judge reads only the first-person contexts.
valence_third_person.takeaway: On the third-person prompt the checkpoints compress toward neutral: they span 2.18 valence points against 4.44 on their own self-report, and every within-model spread widens because the reply invents a character rather than reporting a state.
